<feature feature-id="CC-0081">
  <title>Restrict rotation CronJob ServiceAccount to read-only</title>
  <description># GitHub Issue #190: Restrict rotation CronJob ServiceAccount to read-only and let operator handle Secret writes

**Category**: security | **Scope**: Medium

**Description**: Refactor the fernet/credential key rotation architecture so that the CronJob ServiceAccount only has read access to the key Secrets. The CronJob should compute the new key set and output it (e.g., to a temporary ConfigMap or annotation), and the operator's reconcile loop should detect the output and perform the actual Secret update using its own privileged ServiceAccount.

**Motivation**: The current rotation CronJob's Role grants get and patch on fernet-keys or credential-keys Secrets. If the CronJob pod is compromised via a supply chain attack on the Keystone image, the attacker can write arbitrary fernet keys enabling token forgery. Separating compute (CronJob) from write (operator) follows least-privilege principles.

**Affected Areas**:
- `operators/keystone/internal/controller/reconcile_fernet.go`
- `operators/keystone/internal/controller/reconcile_credential.go`

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [ ] CronJob ServiceAccount has only read access to key Secrets
- [ ] Operator reconciler detects rotation output and performs the Secret update
- [ ] Rotation workflow functions identically from an end-user perspective
- [ ] Unit test verifies CronJob RBAC does not include patch/update verbs on Secrets
- [ ] E2E test verifies key rotation completes successfully with the new architecture

---
Source: https://github.com/C5C3/forge/issues/190</description>

  <implementation-notes>Architecture (Feature ID: CC-0081) — split CronJob compute from operator-owned write-to-production.

ASCII Architecture Diagram:

  +------------------+            +-----------------------+
  | CronJob Pod (SA: |  PATCH     | Staging Secret        |
  | fernet-rotate)   +----------->|  {name}-fernet-keys   |
  | RBAC:            | (data +    |    -rotation          |
  |   get main       |  annotation|  label: rotation-     |
  |   get/patch stg  |  ...)      |  target=fernet-keys   |
  +--------+---------+            |  owner: Keystone      |
           ^                      +-----------+-----------+
           |                                  |
           | read-only Secret volume          | watch (secretToKeystoneMapper)
           |                                  v
  +--------+------------------+    +-----------------------+
  | Production Secret         |<---+ Operator Reconcile    |
  |  {name}-fernet-keys       |    | (SA: keystone-op)     |
  | (PATCHed ONLY by operator)|    |  1. applyRotationOut  |
  +---------------------------+    |  2. validate keys     |
                                   |  3. PATCH main        |
                                   |  4. DELETE staging    |
                                   +-----------------------+

Data Flow:
  1. Reconcile: ensureStagingSecret (create empty, owner-ref)
  2. Reconcile: applyRotationOutput — if staging has completion annotation, validate+PATCH main+DELETE staging
  3. Reconcile: ensureRBAC (Role: get on main, get/patch on staging)
  4. Reconcile: ensureCronJob (SECRET_NAME=staging)
  5. CronJob: rotate in emptyDir → (credential only) migrate DB → PATCH staging Secret with data+annotation
  6. Watch event from staging Secret PATCH → Reconcile → applyRotationOutput (step 2) → production Secret updated
  7. Kubelet projects updated Secret into API pods → new keys active

Key design decisions:
  - STAGING SECRET (not ConfigMap): keys are sensitive material; Secret-typed resources get k8s RBAC isolation that ConfigMaps do not.
  - EMPTY-CREATED BY OPERATOR: the CronJob only needs `patch`, never `create` or `delete` — narrower verb surface.
  - ANNOTATION AS COMMIT MARKER: prevents the operator from observing a half-written staging Secret.
  - OPERATOR-SIDE VALIDATION: defense in depth — even a compromised CronJob cannot push malformed keys.
  - VALIDATION RULE 'count <= MaxActiveKeys+1': tolerates the transient state keystone-manage produces between adding the new primary and pruning the oldest key.
  - OPERATOR ALREADY HAS patch/delete ON SECRETS: no new +kubebuilder:rbac markers needed (REQ-010).
  - WATCH PATH UNCHANGED: secretToKeystoneMapper already enqueues Keystones for owned Secrets via isOwnedBy; staging Secret just rides that path (task 2.6 is verification, not new wiring).

Pitfalls to avoid:
  - Do NOT forget the completion-annotation gate. Without it, reconcile can race the CronJob's writes and see a half-populated staging Secret.
  - Do NOT relax validation to 'len(keys) == MaxActiveKeys' exactly — keystone-manage transiently produces N+1 between add and prune.
  - Do NOT add `list` or `watch` on Secrets to the CronJob Role — the CronJob reads via projected volume.
  - RoleRef on RoleBinding is IMMUTABLE — existing code already guards with `if rb.RoleRef.Name == ''`, preserve that check.
  - For CREDENTIAL rotation, credential_migrate MUST run before the staging PATCH — the DB is re-encrypted with the new primary key and the production Secret update must follow shortly after to minimize the decryption-failure window (REQ-008, REQ-011).
  - CronJob lacks `delete` on staging Secret — if a past rotation's staging Secret is left over, the OPERATOR (not the CronJob) must delete it on successful apply (task 2.3 handles this).

Existing patterns reused:
  - Sub-reconciler condition contract with ObservedGeneration (sub-reconciler-condition-contract-with-observedgeneration.md)
  - Kubernetes event emission alongside condition setting (kubernetes-event-emission-alongside-condition-setting-with-fakerecorder-test-ass.md)
  - Manual Get/Create/Update with SetControllerReference (manual-getcreateupdate-with-setcontrollerreference.md)
  - Shared restrictedSecurityContext helper for PSS (unchanged — CronJob container still uses it)
  - Chainsaw E2E test suite structure (chainsaw-e2e-test-suite-structure-with-jmespath-condition-assertions.md)
  - Immutability verification test for map-returning pure functions — applies to rotation_staging helpers</implementation-notes>
</feature>

  <stories>
    <story title="Security engineer restricts CronJob SA to read-only on key Secrets">As a security engineer, I want the Fernet and credential rotation CronJob ServiceAccounts to have NO write verbs on the key Secrets, so that a supply-chain compromise of the Keystone image cannot forge tokens by writing arbitrary Fernet or credential keys to the production Secret</story>
    <story title="Operator applies rotated keys from the staging Secret to the production Secret">As a operator reconciler, I want to detect a completed rotation output produced by the CronJob and apply it to the production keys Secret using the operator ServiceAccount, so that the write path to the production Secret is owned by the operator, not by the rotation job</story>
    <story title="Operator rejects malformed or tampered rotation output">As a operator reconciler, I want to validate the staging Secret content before applying it to the production Secret, so that a compromised CronJob that writes malformed or out-of-policy keys into the staging Secret still cannot corrupt the production Secret</story>
    <story title="CronJob writes rotated keys to a dedicated staging Secret">As a rotation CronJob, I want to write the rotated key set to a dedicated per-Keystone staging Secret over the Kubernetes API using its own narrowly-scoped ServiceAccount, so that compute (the CronJob) is separated from write-to-production (the operator), preserving least-privilege</story>
    <story title="Operator owns the staging Secret lifecycle">As a operator reconciler, I want to create the staging Secret eagerly (empty) with an owner reference, and to delete it automatically after a successful apply or on Keystone deletion, so that the CronJob can only PATCH an existing, operator-owned Secret (never `create`), and stale staging Secrets do not accumulate</story>
    <story title="End-user observes an unchanged rotation workflow">As a end-user / cluster admin, I want the externally observable behavior of key rotation to remain the same after this refactor, so that upgrading the operator does not require changes to my runbooks or alerting</story>
    <story title="Developer writes a Reference doc for the split-compute-write architecture">As a developer, I want the reconciler reference documentation to describe the staging Secret, the completion annotation, validation rules, and the new RBAC boundaries, so that future maintainers understand why the CronJob does not have write access on the production Secret</story>
    <story title="Developer writes a How-to guide for rotating manually under the new architecture">As a developer / operator, I want a how-to guide for triggering manual rotation and for recovering from a rejected rotation, so that I can safely trigger and audit rotation without reading the Go source</story>
  </stories>
  <requirements>
    <requirement id="REQ-001" priority="SHALL">The Fernet rotation Role SHALL grant only the `get` verb on the production Fernet keys Secret (no `patch`, `update`, `create`, or `delete`).</requirement>
    <requirement id="REQ-002" priority="SHALL">The credential rotation Role SHALL grant only the `get` verb on the production credential-keys Secret.</requirement>
    <requirement id="REQ-003" priority="SHALL">The rotation Role SHALL grant `get` and `patch` on a dedicated staging Secret scoped by `resourceNames`, and SHALL NOT grant `create` or `delete` on it.</requirement>
    <requirement id="REQ-004" priority="SHALL">The operator SHALL create an empty, owner-referenced staging Secret for each key-family (fernet, credential) on every reconcile.</requirement>
    <requirement id="REQ-005" priority="SHALL">The operator SHALL apply rotated keys from the staging Secret to the production Secret ONLY when the staging Secret carries annotation `forge.c5c3.io/rotation-completed-at` with a valid RFC3339 timestamp.</requirement>
    <requirement id="REQ-006" priority="SHALL">The operator SHALL validate rotation output before applying and SHALL reject invalid output without mutating the production Secret.</requirement>
    <requirement id="REQ-007" priority="SHALL">The Fernet rotation script `fernet_rotate.sh` SHALL PATCH the staging Secret (not the production Secret) and SHALL include the `forge.c5c3.io/rotation-completed-at` annotation in the PATCH payload.</requirement>
    <requirement id="REQ-008" priority="SHALL">The credential rotation script `credential_rotate.sh` SHALL behave symmetrically to `fernet_rotate.sh` but SHALL continue to run `credential_rotate` followed by `credential_migrate` BEFORE the staging-Secret PATCH.</requirement>
    <requirement id="REQ-009" priority="SHALL">The operator SHALL watch the staging Secret so that a completed rotation triggers reconcile within one controller-runtime event loop iteration.</requirement>
    <requirement id="REQ-010" priority="SHALL">The operator SHALL expose RBAC verbs `get`, `list`, `watch`, `patch`, `update`, `delete` on `core/secrets` in its existing ClusterRole/Role (no changes needed).</requirement>
